fear_greed.commentary: The index sits in fear at 35, down a point from yesterday's 36 but well above the extreme-fear reading near 17 a week ago and a few points above 30 a month ago.

markets.summary: Stocks snapped a three-day winning streak as a historic drop in Alphabet after its quarterly results revived worries about the payoff from heavy AI spending: the Nasdaq fell 1.38% to 26,184.72, the S&P 500 0.30% to 7,720.39 and the Dow 0.25% to 52,342.56, with Caterpillar also weighing. Tech carried the losses, with chip stocks sliding, though Nvidia's 0.8% dip to $213.66 was milder than the Nasdaq's. Small caps went the other way, as the Russell 2000 rose 1.01% to 2,859.22 and stays above its 40-week average, a sign the selling was concentrated in a few giants. The 10-year Treasury yield eased back just under 5%, to about 4.99%. Gold futures slipped 0.5% to $4,031.40 and silver futures fell 2.4% to $52.19, down about 14% over the past month; both remain below their 40-week averages, and silver's RSI near 28 is now in oversold territory.

stories.headline: JPMorgan lifts SpaceX price target to $500 from $240
stories.summary: JPMorgan kept an Overweight rating and more than doubled its 2027 and 2028 estimates, citing a faster compute buildout, while warning that a lot has to go right for SpaceX to hit those numbers.

stories.headline: Cameco reports Q3 results before Friday's open as uranium-price lag tests execution
stories.summary: Analysts expect 23 cents a share on about $528 million in revenue; investors want to see higher uranium prices start reaching earnings after production disruptions and cost pressures, with estimates cut sharply in recent weeks.

stories.headline: Report on alleged Chinese spy probe touches Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
stories.summary: The New York Times reported US intelligence concluded an executive at Singapore's Megaspeed, suspected of helping China get restricted Nvidia chips, was also gathering intelligence for Beijing and had a close relationship with Huang; Huang told Bloomberg Nvidia's dealings with Megaspeed were ordinary business.

weather.summary: Moisture from Tropical Storm Vance keeps a heavy rain threat over west and central Texas and southeastern New Mexico into Friday, with several inches possible, before storms spread across the Plains and Lower Mississippi Valley Saturday. Tropical Pacific moisture brings flood-prone rain to southern California and the Southwest Friday and through the weekend, especially south-central Arizona, while a deep low off the Pacific Northwest drops over a foot of snow on the highest mountains and spreads rain and mountain snow across the West Saturday.
